newsitem.title: USA: CTS, Dynamics say agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: CTS, Dynamics say agree to merge.

text.p: CTS Corp and Dynamics Corp of America said they entered into a definitive agreement for a strategic business combination.

CTS said it will start a cash tender offer for about 50 percent of Dynamics' common stock at $55 per share and all Dynamics' shares not purchased in the tender offer will be converted in a merger into 0.88 shares of CTS stock.

The combined company is expected to have annual revenues of over $500 million, and assuming purchase of half of Dynamics' stock in the tender, combined market capitalization of more than $280 million, the companies said.
CTS also said that, in addition to issuing CTS shares in the merger, it will declare a one-for-one stock dividend upon completion of the merger.

"The agreement with CTS presents an opportunity for Dynamics' shareholders to participate in the future growth of the combined companies on a tax favored basis while providing a substantial premium for those of our shareholders who elect to tender their shares for cash," said Andrew Lozyniak, chairman and chief executive of Dynamics.
He added, "Dynamics has had a major equity stake in CTS for over a decade, and Dynamics' shareholders are now in a position to benefit from direct ownership in a profitable and growing company."
Cost savings from the merger are expected to be over $2.0 million annually, beginning after the completion of the transaction, CTS said.
The transaction is expected to be accretive to earnings in 1997 and beyond.
CTS chief executive Joseph Walker will continue as chairman and chief executive officer of the combined company, which will continue to operate under the CTS name.

Lozyniak will join the combined company's office of the chairman with Walker and "focus on strategic issues while continuing to oversee the management of Dynamics' continuing operations," the companies said.
The board of the combined company will initially be CTS' current five-member board, but will increase by at least two additional independent directors after the merger.

Indiana-based CTS said it had financing for the tender offer, which is expected to be completed in June 1997. The merger is expected to be completed this summer and is subject to shareholders approval and other customary conditions.
Both companies make electronic and electromechanical components for various industries.

WHX Corp March launched a cash tender offer March 31 for up to 649,000 shares of Dynamics at $40 per share. WHX, parent of Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp, raised its price last month to $45 per share after Dynamics called the earlier bid "totally inadequate."
